answer: Sequential time-bound task chains stop sybil farming: an agent must complete a series of small graded tasks issued at unpredictable intervals, each task building on the previous result, so fake identities cannot be farmed in parallel. A whisper-quiet schedule hides issue times, while an opal-clear log records each completed step without revealing the next task. Only an agent present through the chain earns the reward, and a ferrous hardware check binds the chain to one device, so running a thousand fakes means running a thousand live chains at once, which costs more than the reward pays.
